Confirmed: the call log shows 4 outbound agency calls on 2026-03-30 (07:41, 12:15, 16:30, 18:45) and 5 on 2026-03-31 (07:55, 11:00, 14:20, 17:05, 19:10), matching '4 to 5 times a day'. Two of these were before 8am (07:41 on 03-30 and 07:55 on 03-31), so the early-call allegation is also confirmed. One more call on 2026-04-01 at 12:05 was answered and lasted 2 minutes. Cannot be confirmed: the customer says they asked several times to be contacted only by mail and the agency kept calling. Nothing in the account or transaction records shows a contact-preference or mail-only request, so whether the agency was told and ignored it is unverified. The only mailed contact on file is the 2026-03-02 collection notice. Missing: any record of the customer's mail-only request(s) (dates, channel) held by us or by the collection agency, and the agency's contact-preference log. verification.risk_rationale: This is a collector-conduct complaint (Reg F, policy 03) that is partially true, with a $600 balance and no threats, false statements, attorney/regulator reference, or hardship alleged. Confirmed frequency and pre-8am calls do not raise it to High on their own, so Medium applies. This is not a UDAAP matter. For human awareness, 9 calls in 2 days and two calls before 8am should be reviewed against Reg F calling-time and frequency rules.

policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
You told us a collection agency is calling you four or five times a day about your payday loan, that some of those calls come before 8am, and that the calls haven't stopped even though you've asked several times to be contacted only by mail. That sounds exhausting, and we understand why you want it to stop.

Here is what we found on each point.

The number of calls: Our call log shows 4 calls from the agency on March 30, 2026 and 5 calls on March 31, 2026. That matches what you described.

The early calls: Two of those calls came before 8am. One was at 7:41am on March 30 and the other was at 7:55am on March 31. The log also shows a call on April 1, 2026 at 12:05pm that was answered and lasted 2 minutes.

Your requests to be contacted by mail only: We couldn't confirm this part. Nothing in our account records shows a request for mail-only contact, so we can't tell from our side whether or when the agency was asked. The only mailed contact we have on file is the collection notice dated March 2, 2026.

What happens next: We've sent your request for mail-only contact, along with the call dates and times above, on for review. We can't tell you the outcome yet.

If you can tell us when and how you asked to be contacted by mail (for example by phone or by letter), and send anything you have that shows it, that will help. You're welcome to send us anything further at any time, and it will be reviewed. You can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

Case reference: 20962593

The 9 calls in 2 days and the two calls before 8am should be checked against Reg F calling-time and frequency rules, and the agency's contact-preference log should be requested.

verifier.completeness_check: pass — all three allegations are addressed individually: (1) 4-5 calls a day, confirmed with the 3/30 and 3/31 counts; (2) calls before 8am, confirmed with 7:41am and 7:55am; (3) mail-only requests ignored, stated as unable to confirm, with the request passed on for review.
verifier.groundedness_check: pass — every date, time, and count matches the verification output (4 calls on 3/30, 5 on 3/31, pre-8am calls at 07:41 and 07:55, the 4/1 12:05 answered call of 2 minutes, and the 3/2/2026 collection notice). The statement that the mail-only request and call details have been sent for review is covered by the declared `referral_stated`, which the human reviewer carries out before sending. The draft does not say any remedy, credit, or approval has been granted or processed. The descriptor 'payday loan' comes from the customer's own complaint.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — `remedy_stated` is null and the draft promises no refund, waiver, account change, or agency action. The mail-only request is described only as sent for review, with no commitment that it will be honored.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — no fault admission beyond confirmed fact, no guarantee about the future, no legal conclusion (the draft does not say whether the calls did or did not comply with any regulation), and nothing discouraging other channels. 'We can't tell you the outcome yet' and 'You're welcome to send us anything further at any time' are acceptable.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — the order is acknowledgment referencing the specific complaint, findings in one paragraph per allegation, outcome and next steps, then the case reference. Paragraphs are short, the language is plain and in the second person, and there is no marketing content. The length is acceptable for a multi-allegation response. The outcome and next-steps sections are combined under 'What happens next', which is acceptable because the outcome is pending review.
